grammar_concept.title: Articles: a, an, the, and no article
grammar_concept.rule: Use "a"/"an" to mention something for the first time or to classify it (not a specific one); use "the" when both speaker and listener know exactly which one you mean; use no article at all for general plurals and uncountable nouns.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: "a/an" = one thing, not specific yet. "the" = a specific thing we both already know. No article = talking about something in general.
grammar_concept.example: I saw a dog in the park. The dog was very friendly. I love dogs in general.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Vi um cão no parque. O cão era muito simpático. Adoro cães em geral.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Em português usa-se o artigo definido muito mais vezes do que em inglês — "Gosto do café", "A vida é difícil", "Falo português" usam artigo, mas as traduções corretas em inglês NÃO levam "the": "I like coffee", "Life is difficult", "I speak Portuguese". Um falante de português tende a colocar "the" a mais em frases gerais.
grammar_concept.correction: Não use "the" para falar de algo em geral (coffee, life, love, Portuguese, dogs). Só use "the" quando se refere a uma coisa específica e concreta que já foi mencionada ou que é óbvia pelo contexto.
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Numa conversa: "I don't drink coffee in the evening" (café em geral) vs. "Can you pass me the coffee?" (o café específico que está na mesa).

vocabulary.definition_en: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
example_sentences: Can you give me some advice?

vocabulary.definition_en: facts or details about something (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
example_sentences: I need more information about the course.

vocabulary.definition_en: chairs, tables, beds and other objects in a room (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
example_sentences: We bought some new furniture for the living room.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: I love ___ music.
exercises.explanation: Falar de música em geral não leva artigo nenhum em inglês.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir diretamente do português ("Adoro a música") leva a colocar "the" a mais nesta frase.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence: I saw a cat in the garden. ___ cat was black and white.
exercises.explanation: Na segunda menção, ambos já sabem exatamente de que gato se fala → usa-se "the".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Repetir "a" na segunda menção é um erro comum — depois da primeira vez, se já se sabe qual é, usa-se "the".

correct_answer: an opinion or suggestion about what someone should do (never used with 'a' or in the plural)
exercises.explanation: "Advice" é incontável em inglês — nunca "an advice" nem "advices".

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the speaker's sister give?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "My sister gave me some really good advice about the interview."
exercises.transcript: My sister gave me some really good advice about the interview. She said I should arrive early and bring a copy of my CV.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "Before you buy furniture for a new flat, make a list. You don't need much information — just measure the rooms and know your budget." What should you measure before buying furniture?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "measure the rooms".

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Preciso de alguns conselhos sobre o novo emprego."
correct_answer: I need some advice about the new job.
I need some advice about my new job.
exercises.explanation: "Conselhos" (plural em português) traduz-se por "advice", que em inglês nunca tem plural.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir "conselhos" como "advices" é um erro muito comum — "advice" nunca leva -s.

lesson.title: A, An, The — or Nothing at All

steps.content: The choice between "a" and "an" depends on the SOUND that follows, not the spelling: "an hour" /ən ˈaʊə/ (the h is silent), but "a university" /ə ˌjuːnɪˈvɜːsəti/ (starts with a /j/ sound, even though "u" is a vowel letter).

steps.prompt: Describe your living room, saying what furniture is in it and where each piece is — without using "the" when talking about furniture in general.
Write 5 sentences giving someone advice, using "advice" and "information" correctly (no "a", no plural).
